research_rationale: EO 12648 (53 FR 30637, signed 1988-08-11, published 1988-08-15) is a one-section order. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12648.txt, page 7 of the August 15, 1988 issue; its heading names Executive Order 12648 of August 11, 1988, 'Relating to the Implementation of the Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction'). The preamble recites that the Convention entered into force for the United States on July 1, 1988 and that the order is issued under section 7 of the International Child Abduction Remedies Act; section 1 designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform the acts needed to execute the Central Authority's functions. The held text has no sunset, condition, deadline or termination language. The current predicate uses the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches, because the U.S. Code release-point zip (sha256 c6122974e951003437ece5a998aa7c0b2cdc0f5703dfc78d6135e1fc9e729142) is held only as a custody record; the Code note printing the order under 22 U.S.C. 9006 note is therefore a lead I read but do not cite as a source. Coverage notes read: current-law:usc covers the U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected); current-law:ecfr is an eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 plus GovInfo CFR bulk XML; later-events:ofr_catalog covers disposition notes of 6,941 OFR catalog records and operative sentences in 17,746 saved order texts. The three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) found no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes the order, so no later event is attached. The held texts that cite the number are the order's own Federal Register text and the 1989 codification snapshot only. This is a claim on the held official Federal Register text; the 2026 predicate rests on the Code note and the bounded searches, not on a consolidated agency source.
savings_reason: No revocation, amendment or supersession of the order appears in the held sources and the order has no savings provision of its own, so there is no surviving-effects question; the three bounded searches returned no later instrument.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists in the held evidence: the order's own text has no own-terms end, no later held instrument names it as amended, revoked or superseded (current-law:usc 1 hit, which is the Code note printing the order; current-law:ecfr 0 hits; later-events:ofr_catalog 0 hits), and the only other held text citing the order number is the 1989 codification snapshot. A designation by order is not ended by the passage of time or by performance.
scope_check: One clause covers the whole operative text: section 1, which both designates the Department of State as the Central Authority and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform lawful acts necessary to execute the Central Authority's functions. The preamble paragraphs are recitals, not commands, and the held text of the order is complete (one section and the signature block).
independent_command_check: Section 1 contains two linked commands, the designation and the standing authorization of the Secretary of State. Neither is a one-time act with a completion event; the authorization is a standing grant and the order sets no report, deadline or implementation date that could be mistaken for an end.
savings_check: The order has not been revoked, so no savings clause is engaged and no residual effect needs tracking; the held text contains no savings provision.

research_rationale: EO 12916 (59 FR 25779, signed 1994-05-13) implements the BECC and North American Development Bank agreement and the community adjustment and investment provisions of the NAFTA Implementation Act. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12916.txt, an OCR text layer, read against EO 13380). The inventory is sections 1-11 in 18 clauses. EO 13380 (signed 2005-06-17, no separate effective date, so effective on signing; 70 FR 35509) inserted words in section 1; struck section 2 and inserted a new section 2; struck subsections 3(a), 3(b) and 3(c), the designation (d), and replaced representatives in what remains; replaced Advisory Committee in section 6; and changed Members to members in section 7(c). Under the owner's strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 clauses whose words are replaced continue as amended (sections 1, 3(d), 6, 7(c)). The original sections 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3(a), 3(b) and 3(c) were struck and are not carried into replacement text, so those six clauses are recorded as terminated on 2005-06-17 by express amendment; a human reviewer should note the substance of section 2 changed. Sections 4, 5, 7(a), 7(b), 8, 9, 10 and 11 are not touched by any held instrument. EO 14354 (2025-09-29) continues the Good Neighbor Environmental Board under Executive Order 12916 until September 30, 2027, recorded as a continuation event on section 10. Current predicate: own-text route: the order's own held Federal Register text read with the three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog; U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09, eCFR point-in-time 2026-10-14, OFR catalog of 6,941 records); the Code extracts are leads only because the release-point zip is held only as a custody record; checked through 2026-10-14. The bounded searches found no revocation. Text relied on is the held official Federal Register text for the order, EO 13380 and EO 14354.
savings_reason: The order has not been revoked; the only held amendment is EO 13380, and the held text has no savings provision, so no surviving-effects question arises beyond the continuing clauses.
earlier_end_check: Earlier ends tested: EO 13380 (2005-06-17) is the only held instrument that amends the order and it ends sections 2(a)-(c) and 3(a)-(c) by striking them; the continuation orders (EO 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109, 14354) do not amend it; nothing held revokes or supersedes it (bounded searches: usc 5 hits, ecfr 0, ofr_catalog 3 hits, all EO 13380 or continuation orders). The text of the later U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement implementing act is not held and the claim does not rest on it; no held source shows the section 543 delegations repealed.
scope_check: Inventory: 18 clauses for sections 1, 2(a)-(c), 3(a)-(d), 4, 5, 6, 7(a)-(c), 8, 9, 10 and 11, matching the held text; the preamble is a recital of authority.
independent_command_check: Sections 4-6 are standing delegations, section 7 creates the Finance Committee, sections 8-9 route advice and reports through it, and section 10 delegates continuing authority; none is a one-time act with a completion event.
savings_check: The order has not been revoked, so no savings clause is engaged; the held text contains none.

research_rationale: EO 12985 (61 FR 1209, signed 1996-01-11) establishes the Armed Forces Service Medal. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12985.txt): section 1 establishes the medal for members who on or after June 1, 1992 take part in a significant U.S. military operation and meet no foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action; section 2 provides design approval and award by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation as to the Coast Guard, with precedence before the Humanitarian Service Medal; section 3 limits award to operations with no other service medal and allows one medal with devices; section 4 allows posthumous award. The text has no sunset, deadline or condition. Later instruments found in the held texts that cite the number: EO 13286 section 20 (signed 2003-02-28, effective 2003-03-01 under its section 92) replaces the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security in section 2; EO 13154 section 2 (2000-05-03) and EO 13289 section 3 (2003-03-12) each begin Notwithstanding section 3 of Executive Order 12985 and keep members who qualified through Kosovo service or terrorism-related operations qualified, while allowing the Kosovo Campaign Medal or the Global War on Terrorism medals in lieu. These are an amendment and exceptions, recorded as later events on sections 2 and 3; none revokes or supersedes a clause. The dossier's EO 12977 record carries EO 13286 section 23 text, and EO 12977 predates this order, so it is not an event. Current predicate: own-text route: the order's own held Federal Register text read with the three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog; U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09, eCFR point-in-time 2026-10-14, OFR catalog of 6,941 records); the Code extracts are leads only because the release-point zip is held only as a custody record; checked through 2026-10-14. The bounded searches found no revocation.
savings_reason: The order has not been revoked or superseded; the held text has no savings provision, so there is no surviving-effects question.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists. The only held later instruments naming the order are EO 13286 section 20, EO 13154 section 2 and EO 13289 section 3; the OFR catalog edges (EO 13286 amendment; EO 13154 and EO 13289 cross-references) show no revocation or supersession. EO 12977 is not an event (see rationale).
scope_check: Five inventory clauses cover the four held sections: section 1, section 1(b), section 2, section 3, section 4. The inventory is complete.
independent_command_check: Each section is a standing rule for awarding a continuing medal, not a one-time task; the order sets no report or implementation deadline. EO 13154 and EO 13289 relax section 3 only for the persons and service they describe.
savings_check: The order has not been revoked, so no savings clause is engaged; the held text contains none.

research_rationale: EO 13549 (75 FR 51609, signed 2010-08-18, published 2010-08-23) establishes the Classified National Security Information Program for State, Local, Tribal and Private Sector (SLTPS) entities. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13549.txt, six pages, 21,253 characters). The inventory (61 clauses after one correction) follows the order's own structure: section 1 (sections 1.1-1.3 and paragraphs (a)-(j)), section 2 (the Secretary of Homeland Security as Executive Agent), section 3 (the SLTPS Policy Advisory Committee, paragraphs (a)-(d)), section 4 (Executive Agent duties (1)-(6) and paragraphs (b)-(d)), section 5 (definitions (a)-(m)), section 6 (general provisions (a)-(i)) and section 7 (effective date). The dossier inventory also carried a fragment, sec6-b-13526, which is only the closing word of the list of authorities in section 6(b); an inventory correction merges it into section 6(b) and restates every other span unchanged. Later instruments: none of the held texts that cite the number amends, revokes or supersedes the order. EO 13587 (section 7(b) and (c)), EO 13636, EO 13691 (which amends EO 12829, not this order), EO 13764 (a civil-service rule referring to the order) recite it; EO 13591 and EO 13652 print 'Executive Order 13549, as amended' for the SLTPS Policy Advisory Committee but no held instrument amends the order, and the OFR catalog lists only continuation and cross-reference edges. The eight biennial Federal Advisory Committee Act continuation orders (EO 13591, 13652, 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109, 14354) continue the Committee created by section 3; EO 14354 (signed 2025-09-29) continues it until September 30, 2027, which covers 2026-10-14. They are listed as later events on section 3 and are not amendments. Section 7 makes the order effective 180 days after August 18, 2010 (2011-02-14) except section 3, which was effective at once; section 7 is therefore recorded as terminated by its own terms on 2011-02-14 while the provisions it dates continue. Current predicate: the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches, whose coverage notes I read (U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time 2026-10-14; OFR catalog of 6,941 records and 17,746 saved order texts). The Code extracts (the note under 50 U.S.C. 3161, 6 U.S.C. 662 and 124h-1 and their References in Text notes, which still cite the order) are leads I read; the release-point zip is held only as a custody record, so none is cited as a source. The bounded searches found no revocation. The text relied on is the held official Federal Register text; no transcription is used. The implementing directive that section 1.2 directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to issue within 180 days is not held, and the held evidence does not show whether it was issued; see the independent-command check.
savings_reason: The order has not been revoked or superseded; the continuation orders and cross-references are not savings provisions, and the held text has no savings provision of its own, so there is no surviving-effects question beyond the clauses recorded as operative.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists in the held evidence. The order has no sunset in its own terms except that section 7 fixes its effective date. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends it: the OFR catalog edges with EO 13549 as target are cross-reference notes from EO 12333, 12829, 12968, 13467, 13526, 13591, 13636 and 13691 and continuation notes from EO 13652, 13708 and 13811, none of which is a change provision; EO 13587, 13636, 13691 and 13764 mention the order without a change provision (the dossier's 'cited by number, no change provision located' for EO 12963, 14045 and 14089 is the continuation-order texts); the three bounded searches returned only mentions and continuations. The phrase 'as amended' in EO 13591 and EO 13652 names no amending instrument and none is held.
scope_check: Inventory: 61 clauses matching the held text after correcting the fragment, with section 1.1-1.3 as one lead clause, paragraphs 1.3(a)-(j), sections 2-4 and their sub-paragraphs, definitions 5(a)-(m) with their sub-items, general provisions 6(a)-(i), and section 7. The dossier fragment sec6-b-13526 is a one-word residue of section 6(b) and is merged into that clause by an inventory correction. Section 3 and section 7 are handled separately because of the committee continuation and the effective-date mechanics.
independent_command_check: Section 1.2 contains a time-limited command: an implementing directive is to be issued by the Secretary of Homeland Security within 180 days of the date of the order. That is a deadline, not an end, and the held evidence does not show performance; it is an independent command inside the lead clause, and the lead clause is decided on its continuing establishment-and-policy command, which does not depend on that directive. Section 4(d)(2) and section 1.3(i) (reconciliation within a reasonable period) are standing duties without a stated completion date.
savings_check: The order has not been revoked, so no savings clause is engaged; the held text contains none.
